name: Constantin Brâncuși

notes.name: Wikipedia · Constantin Brâncuși
notes.q: In 1906, he exhibited for the first time at the salon of the Société Nationale des Beaux-Arts and at the Salon d'Automne.

src.name: Wikipedia · Constantin Brâncuși
src.q: He passed through Vienna, Munich, and Basel, where he stayed for a time, and arrived in Paris on July 14, 1904.

src.name: Wikipedia · Constantin Brâncuși
src.q: From 1908, Brâncuși spent time with artists and writers working in Paris, including Amedeo Modigliani, Fernand Léger, Marcel Duchamp, Henri Rousseau, Guillaume Apollinaire, Alexander Archipenko, and Henri Matisse.

src.name: Wikipedia · Constantin Brâncuși
src.q: In 1910, he met the Hungarian painter Margit Pogány, who was studying in Paris.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Constantin Brâncuși
notes.q: Titled An Exhibition of Original Sculpture, in Bronze, Marble, and Wood, by Constantin Brancusi, of Paris, it brought eight sculptures to 291, the gallery operated by Alfred Stieglitz, from March 12 to April 4, 1914.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Constantin Brâncuși
notes.q: In 1915, he donated works to an exhibition at Bernheim-Jeune that raised money for Polish artists affected by the war.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Constantin Brâncuși
notes.q: His first solo exhibition in the United States, An Exhibition of Original Sculpture, in Bronze, Marble, and Wood, by Constantin Brancusi, of Paris, was held at 291 in New York City from March 12 to April 4, 1914.

src.name: Wikipedia · Constantin Brâncuși
src.q: The exhibition opened in New York on February 17, 1913, traveled to Chicago, and ended in Boston.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Constantin Brâncuși
notes.q: In 1925, the Paris magazine This Quarter published photographs, drawings, and aphorisms by Brâncuși.

src.name: Wikipedia · Constantin Brâncuși
src.q: In October 1923, John Quinn spent about two weeks in Paris and visited Brâncuși.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Constantin Brâncuși
notes.q: In December 1927, De Stijl published photographs of Princess X, Sculpture for the Blind, and other works by Brâncuși.

src.name: Wikipedia · Constantin Brâncuși
src.q: One arrived in New York in 1926 and was taxed by customs officials as a manufactured metal object.

src.name: Wikipedia · Constantin Brâncuși
src.q: In April 1939, he traveled to New York again.

src.name: Wikipedia · Constantin Brâncuși
src.q: The Romanian painters Natalia Dumitresco and Alexandre Istrati arrived in Paris in 1947 with scholarships from the French government.
